title: Microsoft Teams: app centric management of app availability in GCC High
summary: The briefing's rollout facts, migration warnings, licensing context and controls are supported. Two minor clarifications remain: complete the org-wide default path to its switch, and warn that the PowerShell reference gives inconsistent descriptions of the blocking Boolean.

claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams"]; "title": "Microsoft Teams: App centric management in Teams Admin Center to manage the Apps access for tenants, end-users, and groups in GCC High"

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: App centric management replaces app permission policies.
claims.quote: Use the feature if already auto-migrated or manually migrate to app centric management. It replaces app permission policies.

claims.claim: Administrators control app access on a per-app basis.
claims.quote: This functionality lets you specify which users and groups can use each app or a copilot agent and you can control it on a per-app basis.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Everyone makes the app available to all organization users, including new users and guests.
claims.quote: `Everyone` | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Specific users or groups limits access to selected users and groups.
claims.quote: `Specific users or groups` | Only the users and groups that you select can use the app.

claims.claim: Specific users or groups excludes guests even when assigned.
claims.quote: Guests can't use the app if this option is selected and even if guests are assigned to the app.

claims.claim: No one makes the app unavailable to every user.
claims.quote: `No one` | Not available to any user | Same as a blocked app.

claims.claim: Administrators can set default availability for new apps published to the Teams app store.
claims.quote: In addition to defining the availability of an app, you can also control the default app availability of any new apps. You can control it for each type of app.

claims.claim: Previously administrators allowed an app in a policy and assigned that policy to the user.
claims.quote: In the past, to allow access to a user, you'd add the app as an allowed app in a policy and assign that policy to the user.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap says existing customers' permission policies are migrated to maintain existing app availability.
claims.quote: The app permission policies for existing customers are migrated to maintain existing app availability in the tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Automatic migration creates one security group per custom app permission policy.
claims.quote: During the auto migration, one security group is created for each custom app permission policy.

claims.claim: Users assigned to a policy are added to its corresponding security group during migration.
claims.quote: All users currently assigned to an app permission policy are then added to the corresponding security group for that policy.

claims.claim: The migrated groups are assigned to the apps their policies allowed.
claims.quote: These groups are assigned to each app they're allowed in their respective policy, maintaining their app access.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: In the global-allow, custom-block conflict case, automatic migration makes the app available to all tenant users.
claims.quote: There's no change of app permissions during the migration, except where an app is allowed in the global policy but blocked in the custom app permission policy. Here, the app is available to all users of the tenant

claims.claim: For EDU customers the conflict case instead makes the app available to none.
claims.quote: except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.claim: Administrators can modify the conflict-case availability after migration.
claims.quote: Admins can modify this behavior as desired post migration.

claims.claim: Learn says app centric management is not yet available to all organizations.
claims.quote: All organizations don't have the app centric management feature available.

claims.claim: Learn points to MC688930 and roadmap item 151829 for timelines.
claims.quote: For timelines, see Message Center post MC688930 or Microsoft 365 roadmap item 151829.

claims.quote: Starting from April 2025, your tenant is automatically migrated to app centric management.

claims.quote: However, until the migration is complete, you can use the wizard and opt to complete the migration manually.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: After switching, administrators cannot access, edit or use permission policies.
claims.quote: After you switch to this feature, you can't access, edit, or use permission policies.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Migration cannot be reverted.
claims.quote: Once your organization migrates, you can't revert the migration.

claims.claim: Migration changes app access management rather than granting new app data permissions.
claims.quote: After migration, any admin consent to app permissions that was previously granted is retained. App permissions are a different concept from permission policies, which app centric management is replacing.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Changing membership of groups assigned to an app changes access through those groups.
claims.quote: Administrators manage these groups like any others to customize the app centric management assignments, such as adding and removing users or removing the group and replacing it with another group.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Previously blocked apps remain unavailable after migration.
claims.quote: After migration, your blocked apps continue to remain unavailable to users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Previously blocked apps show an unblocked status after migration.
claims.quote: The statuses of such apps show as `unblocked` now

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Previously blocked apps are assigned availability No one after migration.
claims.quote: the apps are assigned to `No one` in the `Available to` column on the Manage apps page.

claims.claim: Learn documents no new autonomous behaviour for app centric management.
claims.quote: Searched: "app centric management" autonomous actions. Read app-centric-management and manage-apps; they describe app access, assignment and migration, not a new autonomous action mechanism.

claims.claim: In rare cases changes take up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell. For more information on PowerShell cmdlets for app availability, see Update-M365TeamsApp.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Scope: Who is affected; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn names Teams Administrator as the role needed to use Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role.

claims.quote: Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.quote: In a Microsoft 365 Government - GCC, GCCH and DoD deployment of Teams, all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default.

claims.where: Scope: Rollout; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Assignments support security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, dynamic user membership groups, nested groups and distribution lists.
claims.quote: The supported group types are security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, dynamic user membership groups, nested groups, and the distribution lists.

claims.claim: Up to 99 users or groups can be added to an app at a time.
claims.quote: You can add up to 99 users or groups at a time to an app.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to reaches per-app availability.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. Select Edit availability. Select the required option from Available to menu.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone sets per-app availability to Everyone.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone
Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.claim: AppAssignmentType supports UsersAndGroups with Users and Groups parameters.
claims.quote: -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add -Users eec823bd-0979-4cf8-9924-85bb6ffcb57d, eec823bd-0979-4cf8-9924-85bb6ffcb57e -Groups 37da2d58-fc14-453e-9a14-5065ebd63a1d

claims.claim: AppAssignmentType also supports Noone.
claims.quote:
### -AppAssignmentType
App availability type.
(Everyone
UsersandGroups
Noone)

claims.claim: Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps reaches the pane containing the third-party default.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. You can then configure the settings in the pane.
claims.fix: Complete controls[1].ui.path and the matching table cell as 'Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps > Let users install and use available apps by default'. The switch label is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management#default-settings-for-app-availability, already cited.

claims.claim: A documented automation call identifying which setting changes this org-wide default is not available.
claims.quote: Searched: "Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings" "DefaultApp" "PrivateApp" "GlobalApp"; Teams org-wide app settings third party apps PowerShell DefaultApp GlobalApp Microsoft apps mapping. Read update-m365unifiedtenantsettings, manage-apps and app-centric-management; no mapping found.

claims.claim: The Microsoft apps and Custom apps settings are in the same Org-wide app settings pane.
claims.quote:
You can then configure the settings in the pane.
Under Microsoft apps, a single control automatically enables users to install and use any available agents and apps by default.
Under Custom apps, turn off or turn on Let users install and use available apps by default option.

claims.claim: Org-wide defaults do not override apps individually assigned to Specific users and groups.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to:
All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you.

claims.claim: Org-wide defaults do not override apps individually saved as Everyone or No one.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to:
All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually.

claims.claim: Org-wide defaults do not apply to blocked apps.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to:
Any blocked apps.

claims.claim: Org-wide defaults apply to existing apps whose availability has not been actively managed.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings apply to:
All the existing apps that you didn't actively manage, that is, you didn't change the availability of.

claims.claim: Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block is a documented route to change the selected app's org-level status.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps.
Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked $true is documented for changing the app's org-level state.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).
claims.fix: Keep the call but append to controls[2].note and the matching table note: 'The reference describes -IsBlocked $true as unblocking in Example 3, but also describes -IsBlocked $false as unblocking in Example 4; its examples do not consistently establish the Boolean polarity. Use the UI when the intended state must be unambiguous.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/update-m365teamsapp.

claims.claim: App status is an app-level control separate from per-user availability.
claims.quote:
App status: It applies at an app-level as allow or block and controls if it's available to any user or not.
Each app contains its access definition using a list of users and groups that you assign to it.

claims.claim: An app must be allowed through all applicable access controls, whereas any one blocking control suffices.
claims.quote: To allow an agent or app, you must do all of the following settings. To block an agent or app, use any one of the following settings:
